Which sections of The New York Times produced the most-viewed articles over the past 30 days, and what topics were those articles about?

## Data source

The data comes from the New York Times **Most Popular API**, using this endpoint:

`https://api.nytimes.com/svc/mostpopular/v2/viewed/30.json`

It returns the 20 most-viewed articles on NYTimes.com over a period of 1, 7, or 30 days. Each article comes with its title, section, byline, publish date, topic tags, and images.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| period | `30` | set in the URL path (the past 30 days) |
| api-key | my NYT API key | stored in the `NYT_API_KEY` environment variable |

The full request, with the key hidden:

```
https://api.nytimes.com/svc/mostpopular/v2/viewed/30.json?api-key=HIDDEN
```

## Setup

```{r}
library(httr2)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

api_key <- Sys.getenv("NYT_API_KEY")
if (api_key == "") {
  stop("NYT_API_KEY is not set. Add it to .Renviron and restart R.")
}
```

The API key is read from my `.Renviron` file, so it does not appear anywhere in this document.

## Pulling the data

```{r}
resp <- request("https://api.nytimes.com/svc/mostpopular/v2/viewed/30.json") |>
  req_url_query(`api-key` = api_key) |>
  req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE) |>
  req_perform()

if (resp_status(resp) != 200) {
  stop("Request failed with status ", resp_status(resp))
}

resp_status(resp)
```

A status of 200 means the request worked.

```{r}
raw <- resp_body_json(resp)
names(raw)
raw$num_results

results <- raw$results
names(results[[1]])
```

The JSON comes back as nested lists. The articles are stored in `results`, one list per article, and each article has `r length(results[[1]])` fields.

## Building the data frames

```{r}
articles <- tibble(
  rank       = seq_along(results),
  title      = map_chr(results, "title", .default = NA_character_),
  section    = map_chr(results, "section", .default = NA_character_),
  subsection = map_chr(results, "subsection", .default = NA_character_),
  byline     = map_chr(results, "byline", .default = NA_character_),
  type       = map_chr(results, "type", .default = NA_character_),
  published  = map_chr(results, "published_date", .default = NA_character_),
  caption    = map_chr(results, list("media", 1, "caption"),
                       .default = NA_character_),
  url        = map_chr(results, "url", .default = NA_character_)
) |>
  mutate(
    published = as.Date(published),
    byline    = sub("^By ", "", byline),
    across(c(subsection, byline, caption), \(x) na_if(trimws(x), ""))
  )

glimpse(articles)
colSums(is.na(articles))
```

`articles` has one row per article.

```{r}
topics <- tibble(
  rank  = seq_along(results),
  topic = map(results, \(a) unlist(a$des_facet))
) |>
  unnest_longer(topic) |>
  filter(!startsWith(topic, "internal-"))

head(topics, 10)
```

`topics` has one row for each topic tag on each article.

## Cleaning notes

- **Nested fields:** `media` is a list of images, and each image has its own list of sizes. I kept only the caption of the first image. The topic tags (`des_facet`) are also a list inside each article, so I put them in a separate long table instead of cramming them into one column.
- **Missing values:** Most articles have an empty `subsection`, and some have no byline or no image. I changed empty text to `NA` and kept every article.
- **Internal tags:** A few articles carry tags that start with `internal-`. These are NYT website settings, not topics, so I removed them.
- **Types and text:** I converted `published_date` from text to a date and removed "By " from the bylines.
- **Fields left out:** IDs, `adx_keywords`, and the people, place, and organization tags, since they don't relate to the question.

## Results

```{r}
articles |>
  mutate(published = format(published, "%b %d")) |>
  select(rank, title, section, published) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r}
by_section <- articles |> count(section, sort = TRUE)

ggplot(by_section, aes(x = n, y = reorder(section, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.4, color = "#1F2933") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(title = "Sections of the 20 most-viewed NYT articles",
       subtitle = "Past 30 days",
       x = "Articles", y = NULL,
       caption = "Source: NYT Most Popular API") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(plot.title.position = "plot",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r}
top_topics <- topics |> count(topic, sort = TRUE) |> head(5)
knitr::kable(top_topics)
```

The `r by_section$section[1]` section had the most articles in the top 20, with `r by_section$n[1]` of `r nrow(articles)`, followed by `r by_section$section[2]` with `r by_section$n[2]`. The most common topic tag was "`r top_topics$topic[1]`," which appeared on `r top_topics$n[1]` articles. The list changes every day, so these results describe the 30 days before `r format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")`.
